blocks.text: BAGUIO CITY — The summer capital’s public museum is undergoing a P30-million facelift as a dispute over ownership has erupted between the Baguio government and some residents, including half of the Baguio Museum Inc. board of trustees. The Baguio City Council was briefed last week on the city’s plans to renovate the interiors of the former Baguio-Mountain Provinces Museum, built in 1975 and opened in 1977. Architect Johnny Degay, the city building officer, told the council during its November 16 session that the museum’s modernization would infuse “stories about Baguio” at every level of the four-story structure that would be redesigned […]...
